{"category":"convention","enforced":true,"name":"Design information lives in the graph, not in documents","statement":"This project does not store design information in documents. What a document would have said belongs in the graph as typed nodes. Anthony's word, 2026-08-15: "we no longer use documents to store info. should be in graph" — and, on the buildup of two feedback files captured only partially, "we can't let this buildup occur again".

ENFORCEMENT IS HIS EXPLICIT ANSWER, NOT AN INHERITED DEFAULT. Asked what should happen if somebody added a markdown file holding design information — good content, tests passing — he chose STOP THE BUILD over advice and over leaving it unstated.

⚠️ THIS RULE OWES A DETECTOR AND CANNOT HAVE ONE YET, because two things must be scoped before a check could tell a violation from ordinary work:

(1) SCOPE. 187 markdown files are tracked outside `docs/design/`. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, COORD.md, REFLOW2.md, README, CHANGELOG and every served SKILL.md are documents, and several are load-bearing instructions the project cannot function without. A check that cannot say which of the 187 are violations would either fail every build or none.

(2) A CONFLICT WITH THE SCHEMA'S OWN DESIGN, measured 2026-08-15 while trying to comply with this rule: `Fragment.content_ref` is described as a "Pointer to the source content (path/hash) RATHER THAN INLINING IT", and Fragment carries no field for a document's text — only title, summary, intent and that pointer. `Artifact.location` and the `DOCUMENTS` edge are built on the same assumption. So reflow2's vocabulary currently presumes documents EXIST and that the graph points AT them; it has no way to absorb prose. Under a literal reading of this rule, `capture-intent`'s own step 3 — which instructs an agent to register a source document as an Artifact with a location — would itself be a violation.

SO THE RULE IS RECORDED AS STATED AND AS ENFORCED, and what it means operationally is the open part. Nothing here softens it: it is his rule and his enforcement choice. What is unresolved is what counts as "design information" versus operating instructions, and whether the graph gains a way to hold prose or the rule scopes around the fact that it cannot."}
